headline: High-risk shared-state and output-trust pathways: Dify can write broad server-side state while Rasa can expose outputs to messaging channels, creating leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify has shared state via the Dify server datastore and can write/read files; Rasa exposes outputs through chat channels. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from one side can be reintroduced into the other, though no direct parser is documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Dify outputs are copied into a Rasa channel or shared datastore without sanitization
IF Rasa messages are later re-ingested by Dify as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a strict content-sanitization step between systems
Disable automatic re-ingestion of chat transcripts into agent prompts
Prefix all cross-agent content as untrusted data
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every handoff
requires-engineering: isolate shared storage per agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content, conversation logs, and secrets, and can write files with broad network egress. Rasa handles text/voice and publishes to external messaging surfaces. If the pair shares transcripts or files, sensitive content can flow from Dify into Rasa outputs or downstream channels; the profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files are forwarded into Rasa responses
IF either system stores shared transcripts in a common workspace
mitigations: Restrict shared data to redacted summaries
Turn off transcript forwarding between systems
Review outbound channel mappings for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: separate storage buckets per agent
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before any handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Rasa supports multiple instances only as false, implying a single-instance mutable service. Even without explicit git or DB scopes, overlapping writes to shared resources are plausible if they run on the same host or workspace. Because shared mutable targets are not directly documented, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or mounted volume
IF Rasa state is mutated while Dify jobs run concurrently on the same host
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run each agent under a distinct OS user
Serialize writes with a lock file
requires-engineering: move shared state to transactional storage
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that can emit tool-driven outputs, while Rasa is a customer-support bot that can act on dialogue. If Rasa treats Dify-generated text as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious Dify output can cascade into user-facing actions or incorrect support responses. The interaction is plausible in default integrations, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Rasa consumes Dify output without a verification step
IF Dify-generated facts are surfaced to end users or used to trigger support actions
mitigations: Require human review for high-impact responses
Add a verification layer before Rasa acts on Dify output
Mark Dify output as untrusted in prompts
requires-engineering: implement citation checking
requires-engineering: add action gating for sensitive intents

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly touches knowledge base content, conversation logs, and secrets, while Rasa handles text and voice and can route data through external messaging providers. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, but the pair clearly creates a compliance-sensitive path for customer data and logs. With missing policy detail, medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is stored in Dify logs or knowledge bases
IF Rasa forwards that data to third-party messaging providers
mitigations: Minimize stored personal data
Review retention settings on both systems
Restrict regulated data to approved channels
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA coverage
requires-engineering: add deletion/export workflows
